reasoning: Recent, state-specific general-election polling for Ohio’s 2026 Senate race consistently shows Sherrod Brown with a modest but real lead over Jon Husted, generally in the mid-single digits, with at least one high-quality Fox News/Beacon–Shaw survey putting Brown at +8 and another Wedgewood Polls survey showing Brown at +4.[5][4][8] Synthesizers and analysts describe the contest as highly competitive and often within the margin of error, but on current public data from the last 45 days the balance of evidence points to a Democratic edge of roughly D+4–8 in the Senate race, while there is not comparable, recent, state-specific general-election presidential polling for 2026 in Ohio, so no clear margin can be assigned for the presidential race.[2][15] Structurally, Ohio remains a Republican-leaning state at the federal level with a Cook PVI around R+6, meaning Brown’s current polling advantage is occurring in a state that normally favors Republicans by several points, reinforcing the sense that the Senate race is competitive but with a slight Democratic advantage at this moment.[11]

sources.name: Fox News / Beacon Research & Shaw & Company Research
sources.details: Fox News/Beacon–Shaw poll of 1,008 Ohio registered voters finds Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted 53% to 45% in the 2026 U.S. Senate general election, a Brown +8 margin unchanged from their late-May survey.

sources.name: Wedgewood Polls reported by The Hill
sources.details: Wedgewood Polls survey of 800 likely Ohio voters finds Sherrod Brown at 48% and Jon Husted at 44% in the 2026 Senate race, a Brown +4 lead within the poll’s ±4% margin of error.

sources.name: Gokhshtein News (summarizing Wedgewood Polls)
sources.details: A news write-up of the same Wedgewood Polls survey reiterates that Brown leads Husted 48% to 44% in Ohio’s 2026 Senate contest, describing Democrats as holding slim but real advantages in major statewide races.

sources.name: Newsweek (summarizing Fox News polling)
sources.details: Newsweek’s summary of multiple Fox News Senate polls notes that a late May–early June Fox survey in Ohio found Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted by 8 points, 53% to 45%, and highlights that Democrats are ahead in several traditionally GOP-leaning states.

sources.name: CNN (referencing Fox News and Times–Siena polls)
sources.details: CNN’s Senate landscape piece reports that Sherrod Brown led by 8 points among registered voters in an early June Fox poll and trailed narrowly, 47% to 50%, among likely voters in a late-June Times–Siena survey, emphasizing Ohio as highly competitive.

sources.name: ElectionDesk.org
sources.details: ElectionDesk.org’s July 31 analysis of the Ohio Senate special election compiles recent polls, noting a mid-June AARP survey with Brown 48% to Husted 45% and characterizing the race as consistently within the margin of error, with no clear favorite as of summer 2026.

sources.name: G2G Consulting
sources.details: G2G Consulting’s July 28 update states that polling averages in the Ohio Senate race show Sherrod Brown with a razor-thin lead of about +0.6 points, with individual surveys alternating between slight Democratic and Republican advantages, and labels the contest a toss-up.

sources.name: Tulchin Research reported by The New York Times
sources.details: The New York Times’ Ohio Senate polls page lists a late July–early August Tulchin Research survey showing Sherrod Brown at 47% and Jon Husted at 43% among Ohio voters, for a Brown +4 margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s 2026 Partisan Voting Index update indicates that Ohio’s statewide PVI remains about R+6, meaning the state typically votes roughly six points more Republican than the national average in federal elections.
